subject: R syntax to compute Fisher Exact Test on data loaded in to Rattle

messages.author: 027e86e2d7290ed1
messages.subject: R syntax to compute Fisher Exact Test on data loaded in to Rattle
parts:
I have come to appreciate the use of the 'Explore' and 'Test' tabs in the Rattle interface.  The ability to rapidly explore distributions and test for significance (K-S and W-R-S) has been of great help.  Most of my analyses use a categorical target ( mostly with binary values of yes/no) - the 'group by target' checkbox seems the 'fast-track' to univariate stats.  The 'Test' tab only supports numeric input variables.  Many of my inputs are also binary (i.e. yes/no) variables and it would be helpful to do Fisher Exact (as input compares to target).  I presume this would be possible by entering the appropriate commands in the R console.  I am posting to see if anyone versed in R could help me with the proper commands/syntax.  Assuming I load into Rattle a file named f.csv with a categorical target T ('yes/no') and a categorical predictor P1 ('yes/no'), what commands would one enter into the R-console to calculate a Fisher's Exact Analysis.

Thank you !!!

This would need ti be checked with the manual page for the fisher.test function in R (do a ?fisher.test in the R Console), but perhaps it is simply:

> fisher.test(table(crs$dataset))

The variable crs$dataset is where Rattle stores the data you have read in from f.csv.

If you do:

> table(crs$dataset)

you should get the relevant counts.

It can then passed on to the fisher.test function, but do check the manual page for the fisher.test to make sure this is what is expected.

Hope that helps.

Regards,
Graham
